{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Development and Option Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Development and Option Agreement (AbbVie as Customer/licensee; Harpoon as counterparty)

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Development and Option Agreement against the playbook. On balance the Agreement is strongly favourable to us on the core commercial architecture: the licence grant to us exceeds the fallback (worldwide exclusive licence, multi-tier sublicensing without consent, and conversion to a non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable grant on expiry under Section 12.1.2); we hold an unconditional 90-day termination-for-convenience right (Section 12.3) with no exit fee; and the only exclusivity/non-compete covenant in the document (Section 5.8) binds Harpoon, not us. There are no minimum purchase commitments, no MFN mechanic, no non-solicitation restriction on us, no liquidated damages payable by us, and no auto-renewal.

Seven items require attention. Two are high severity: (i) the assignment clause (Section 13.4.1) is fully mutual, letting Harpoon assign to an Affiliate or successor without our consent and with no bar on assignment to a Competitor; and (ii) Section 11.5 waives indirect and consequential damages but contains no monetary cap anywhere in the Agreement, leaving direct liability unlimited on both sides. Four medium items concern the open numeric terms in the audit clause (Section 6.11), the absence of any designated court forum notwithstanding the Delaware governing law (Section 13.6), the redacted indemnity triggers in Article 11, and the absence of any performance warranty in Article 10. Two low-severity gaps are missing E&O and cyber insurance in the Section 11.6.1 schedule, and the absence of post-termination transition assistance and data-return obligations on Harpoon.

We note that several provisions are redacted ([***]) — including sub-clauses of Sections 7.1.2 and 12.7, the Article 11 indemnity trigger lists, the general liability limits in Section 11.6.1, the audit variance threshold in Section 6.11, and the arbitration seat and rules in Schedule 13.7.3 — so certain conclusions rest on the visible text only.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 7 Intellectual Property | Sits at or above fallback; no AbbVie IP or data assigned to Harpoon. Joint ownership under 7.1.2 is workable (each Party may Exploit without consent or accounting). Some 7.1.2/12.7 carve-outs redacted. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 13.4.1 / § 13.2 | Mutual no-consent affiliate/successor carve-out and no bar on assignment to a Competitor; fails fallback. |
| High | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 11.5 | Mutual consequential-damages waiver but no monetary cap anywhere; direct liability unlimited. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 5 (5.8) | Only exclusivity covenant runs against Harpoon; no sourcing or non-compete duty on us. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 12 | No LDs, penalties, minimum fees or early-termination fees payable by us. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 5 (5.1.1–5.1.3, 5.3) | Exceeds fallback; paid-up irrevocable grant on expiry (§ 12.1.2). Insolvency trigger (§ 12.4) noted only. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 5 | No non-compete, field-of-use or territory covenant binding us. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12.3 | Unconditional 90-day right, no fee; Harpoon has no convenience right. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 6.11 | Frequency, notice and variance threshold all left open ([***]); permits repeated unannounced audits. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 13.6 / § 13.7 | Delaware law (fallback) but no court forum designated; either Party may elect arbitration under a redacted schedule. |
| Medium | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 11.1–11.2 | Structure meets preferred, but trigger lists are redacted; no verifiable IP, law, data-breach or GN/WM trigger. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | **Deviation** | § 10 | Article 10 contains only Effective-Date reps and covenants; no conformance warranty and no remedy. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 13 | No MFN, best-price or right-to-match mechanic in either direction. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 4 (4.5.1–4.5.2) | No minimum, volume or take-or-pay obligation; we hold sole Manufacture/supply rights. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 10.4 | No solicitation, recruitment or no-hire restriction on us. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 12.1 | No evergreen mechanic; extension requires mutual written amendment (§ 13.9). |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 11.6.1 | No professional liability (E&O) and no cyber/privacy coverage in the schedule. |
| Low | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | § 9.7 / Art. 12 | No wind-down support obligation; § 9.7 return is request-based, allows destruction election, no deadline. |

---

## 3. Proposed redlines (deviations and gaps)

1. **Assignment (§ 13.4.1)** — Limit the no-consent affiliate/successor carve-out to AbbVie, bar assignment by Harpoon to a Competitor, and add one sentence confirming that an AbbVie Change in Control gives Harpoon no termination right. We leave the existing "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" consent standard verbatim, and leave Section 13.2's Harpoon-side Change in Control regime (which is favourable to us) untouched.
2. **Liability cap (after § 11.5)** — Insert a mutual aggregate cap at twelve months' fees, with indemnification, Article 9 confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct expressly uncapped. We are targeting the fallback only; we have not sought the USD 1,000,000 floor or the additional preferred carve-outs.
3. **Audit (§ 6.11)** — Fix the open terms at fallback: once per twelve-month period, fifteen (15) days' prior written notice, and cost on Harpoon unless underpayment exceeds 10%. Qualitative protections (independent firm reasonably acceptable to us, books and records only, confidentiality under § 6.13) are already sound.
4. **Forum (§ 13.6 / § 13.7)** — Replace the party-elected arbitration route with exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts, matching the Delaware governing law already selected. The Senior Officer step, the IP carve-out (§ 13.7.2) and the interim-relief carve-out (§ 13.7.5) are untouched.
5. **Indemnity (§ 11.1–11.2)** — Add four Harpoon-side triggers to Section 11.2 as an additive "without limiting the foregoing" list (third-party IP infringement, Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, Harpoon-caused data breach, Harpoon's gross negligence/willful misconduct) so any equivalent redacted trigger is preserved rather than overwritten; and add one sentence confining our Section 11.1 indemnity to AbbVie-provided content and AbbVie's breach of law. We do not seek the fallback 3x-fees super-cap, as Harpoon's indemnity is presently uncapped in our favour.
6. **Warranty (new § 10.6)** — Insert a fallback-level express warranty: 90-day conformance for software/deliverables and 30 days for Harpoon's Development activities, with repair/replacement, re-performance or refund, plus a narrow override of the "non-refundable" language in Sections 6.1–6.4 so the refund leg is operative. The Section 10.5 disclaimer already preserves express warranties and needs no edit.
7. **Insurance (§ 11.6.1)** — Add Harpoon-only E&O of USD 1M and cyber/privacy of USD 2M to the schedule of minimum limits. Drafted as a Harpoon obligation so as not to create a new mutual burden on us.
8. **Transition (new § 12.11)** — Require Harpoon, on any expiry or termination, to provide at least 90 days of transition assistance and to return AbbVie data within 30 days. The override is confined to the § 9.7(a)–(b) destruction election and timing, preserving Harpoon's one-copy retention proviso and back-up carve-out, and carves out data Harpoon retains rights to under the surviving reversion provisions (including §§ 12.6 and 12.7).

---

## 4. Walk-away items

None of the findings falls into walk-away territory. In particular:

- **IP (critical rule)** — reviewed for walk-away exposure and cleared. The joint ownership created by Section 7.1.2 is workable rather than walk-away, because each Party may Exploit Joint IP without consent or accounting and the only overlays run in our favour; and the Section 12.7.1 reversion is a conditional, royalty-bearing licence of a defined AbbVie Reversion IP set, not an assignment of our IP.
- The two high-severity deviations (assignment mutuality and the absent liability cap) are negotiable positions we should press hard, but neither is identified as a walk-away.
- **Caveat:** the redacted sub-clauses of Sections 7.1.2 and 12.7, and the redacted Article 11 trigger lists, could not be verified. We should reserve judgement on walk-away exposure in those areas until the unredacted text is available.

---

## 5. Next steps

1. **Request unredacted text** for the Article 11 indemnity triggers, Sections 7.1.2 and 12.7 carve-outs, the Section 6.11 variance threshold, the Section 11.6.1 general liability limits, and Schedule 13.7.3 (arbitration seat and rules). Several conclusions above are provisional pending this text, and the indemnity and IP analyses in particular may change.
2. **Issue the eight redlines** in Section 3, with the assignment and liability-cap items marked as our priority asks.
3. **Confirm with Business/Insurance Risk** that Harpoon can procure the E&O and cyber limits, and confirm whether the AbbVie self-insurance right at Section 11.6.3 affects our approach.
4. **Confirm with the deal team** that exclusive Delaware court jurisdiction is preferred over the currently available arbitration election, given the redacted arbitration schedule.
5. **Sequence for negotiation:** treat the compliant findings (licence scope, T4C, exclusivity, non-compete, minimum commitments, MFN, non-solicit, renewal, LDs) as settled and off the table, and hold the fallback positions on audit, warranty, insurance and transition as tradeable if needed to secure the liability cap and the assignment restriction.

*This memo is based solely on the verified findings supplied and the sections cited therein.*"}
